arxiv-2109-08061.title: Invertible Frowns: Video-to-Video Facial Emotion Translation
arxiv-2109-08061.creator: Ian Magnusson, Aruna Sankaranarayanan, Andrew Lippman
arxiv-2109-08061.description: Abstract We present Wav2Lip-Emotion, a video-to-video translation architecture that modifies facial expressions of emotion in videos of speakers. Previous work modifies emotion in images, uses a single image to produce a video with animated emotion, or puppets facial expressions in videos with landmarks from a reference video.

arxiv-2402-16042.title: Enhancement of Entanglement via Josephson Parametric Amplifier in a Dual Cavity-Magnon System
arxiv-2402-16042.creator: Abdelkader Hidki, Abderrahim Lakhfif, Mostafa Nassik, Rizwan Ahmed, Amjad Sohail
arxiv-2402-16042.description: Abstract In the two microwave (MW) cross-shaped cavity magnon system, we describe a method to produce multipartite entanglement and quantum steering. To achieve squeezed states of the magnons, a Josephson parametric amplifier (JPA) creates a squeezed vacuum field that drives the two cavities.

arxiv-2403-03896.title: DART: Implicit Doppler Tomography for Radar Novel View Synthesis
arxiv-2403-03896.creator: Tianshu Huang, John Miller, Akarsh Prabhakara, Tao Jin, Tarana Laroia, Zico Kolter, Anthony Rowe
arxiv-2403-03896.description: Abstract Simulation is an invaluable tool for radio-frequency system designers that enables rapid prototyping of various algorithms for imaging, target detection, classification, and tracking. However, simulating realistic radar scans is a challenging task that requires an accurate model of the scene, radio frequency material properties, and a corresponding radar synthesis function.

arxiv-2403-07135.title: Noninvasive cavity-based charge diagnostic for plasma accelerators
arxiv-2403-07135.creator: S. Bohlen 1,2, O. Kononenko 1, J.-P. Schwinkendorf 1,2, F. Grüner 1,2, D. Lipka 1, M. Meisel 1,2, C.A.J. Palmer 1, T. Staufer 2, K. Põder 1 and J. Osterhoff 1,2
arxiv-2403-07135.description: Abstract The charge contained in an electron bunch is one of the most important parameters in accelerator physics. Several techniques to measure the electron bunch charge exist. However, many conventional charge diagnostics face serious drawbacks when applied to plasma accelerators.

arxiv-2405-19479.title: Participation in the Age of Foundation Models
arxiv-2405-19479.creator: Harini Suresh, Emily Tseng, Meg Young, Mary L. Gray, Emma Pierson, Karen Levy
arxiv-2405-19479.description: Abstract . Growing interest and investment in the capabilities of foundation models has positioned such systems to impact a wide array of services, from banking to healthcare. Alongside these opportunities is the risk that these systems reify existing power imbalances and cause disproportionate harm to historically marginalized groups.

arxiv-2411-11519.title: Transformer networks for Heavy flavor jet tagging
arxiv-2411-11519.creator: A. Hammad, Mihoko M. Nojiri
arxiv-2411-11519.description: Abstract In this article, we review recent machine learning methods used in challenging particle identification of heavy-boosted particles at high-energy colliders. Our primary focus is on attention-based Transformer networks. We report the performance of state-of-the-art deep learning networks and further improvement coming from the modification of networks based on physics insights.

arxiv-2507-00265.title: Examining Reject Relations in Stimulus Equivalence Simulations
arxiv-2507-00265.creator: Alexis Carrillo, Asieh Abolpour Mofrad, Anis Yazidi, Moises Betancort
arxiv-2507-00265.description: Abstract Simulations offer a valuable tool for exploring stimulus equivalence (SE), yet the potential of reject relations to disrupt the assessment of equivalence class formation is contentious. This study investigates the role of reject relations in the acquisition of stimulus equivalence using computational models.

arxiv-2603-10263.creator: Zhanyi Sun, Shuran Song

europmc-pmc2825552.creator: Akcay A, Nguyen Q, Edelstein CL.
europmc-pmc2825552.description: Acute kidney injury (AKI) remains to be an independent risk factor for mortality and morbidity. Inflammation is now believed to play a major role in the pathophysiology of AKI. It is hypothesized that in ischemia, sepsis and nephrotoxic models that the initial insult results in...

pmc-11405391.title: Identification of transcription factors associated with leaf senescence in tobacco
pmc-11405391.creator: Zhenbiao Zhang, Muhammad Shan, Liyu Yang, Songxiao Cao, Jie Wang, Wei Li, Yongfeng Guo
pmc-11405391.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Leaf senescence represents the final stage of leaf development, involving transcription factors (TFs)-mediated genetic reprogramming events. The timing of crop leaf senescence has a major influence on the yield and quality of crop in agricultural production. As important regulator of plant growth, the significance of TFs in the regulation of leaf senescence have been highlighted in various plant species by recent advances in genetics. However, studies on underlying molecular mechanisms are still not adequately explained.

pmc-11712167.title: Our youth, our compass: families walking with younger‐onset dementia shine light on stigma
pmc-11712167.creator: Diana Shulla Cose, Stephanie Fitzgerald, Patti LaFleur, Bree Ruge
pmc-11712167.description: PurposeFor youth walking with a parent’s younger‐onset dementia diagnosis, our voices are the softest, yet our journey is often the hardest. We are helping to open the shades and bring light. We are telling the stories of our Mother’s and our Father’s. We are the survivors who choose to advocate for a more just world for our families.

pmc-12433502.title: KNC nanozyme repairs hypoxia ischemia brain damage through ALOX12 mediated lipid peroxidation inhibition
pmc-12433502.creator: Xiaohua Dong, Dongya Jiang, Shuhan Chen, Ji Tan, Jing Zhao, Xingdan Liu, Ziyi Lu, Kelvin W.K. Yeung, Yun Liao, Xuanyong Liu, Liping Ouyang
pmc-12433502.description: Hypoxia-Ischemia Brain Damage (HIBD) results in a widespread neuronal damage and permanent brain tissue injury due to the severe reactive oxygen species (ROS) boost induced neuroinflammation. In this work, a K doped N-C based nanozyme was fabricated for scavenging ROS. KNC could impair ROS production and M1 polarization in microglia.

pmc-12676572.title: Traumatic brain injury and mortality in older adults with and without pre-injury dementia
pmc-12676572.creator: Helen Lai, Eyal Soreq, Niall J Bourke, Claire Baker, Karl Zimmerman, Megan E Parkinson, Sarah J C Daniels, Edward W Gregg, David Sharp, Lucia M Li
pmc-12676572.description: BackgroundIncidence of traumatic brain injury (TBI) is rising in older adults. Dementia is a common comorbidity and may worsen post-TBI outcomes, but its effects have not been studied.ObjectiveTo compare all-cause mortality following TBI or non-TBI trauma (NTT) and quantify the impacts of age, deprivation and dementia.DesignPopulation-based retrospective cohort study.

pmc-12693670.title: Comparison of Suture Anchor Constructs in Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Reconstruction: Assessing Clinical Outcome and Treatment Cost Variations
pmc-12693670.creator: David Endell, Tim Schneller, Moritz Kraus, Markus Scheibel, Emmanuel Andrès, Moshe Salai
pmc-12693670.description: Background: Cuff reconstructions vary due to different technical approaches by suture anchor manufacturers, as well as different suture construct configurations. Objectives: The main aim of this study is to primarily compare clinical outcomes and secondarily observe cost-effectiveness by assessing suture construct configurations in arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR).

pmc-13342630.title: Database of tensile test results of carbon fibers impregnated with thermoplastic polymer
pmc-13342630.creator: Mikhail Lazarev, Denis Derkach, Fedor Ratnikov, Dilus Chukov, Sergey Gromov, Andrey Stepashkin
pmc-13342630.description: In this study, we present a comprehensive set of experimental data aimed at uncovering the mechanisms and regularities governing the deformation behavior of composites reinforced with continuous carbon fibers (CF) based on thermoplastic polymers. This work describes data extraction techniques that can later be used to optimize the mechanical properties of such structures using neural network models.

pmc-13382340.title: Regulatory T cells promote sensory neuron growth and protect against neurotoxicity
pmc-13382340.creator: Jessica P. Hayes, Sandra Fok, Renee Whan, Gary D. Housley, Gila Moalem-Taylor
pmc-13382340.description: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) maintain immune homeostasis and suppress inflammation, and emerging evidence indicates they also modulate neuronal function and regeneration. Dorsal root ganglion (DRG) sensory neurons transmit pain signals and are damaged by chemotherapeutic agents such as paclitaxel (PTX), leading to neuropathic pain. Although Tregs show therapeutic promise in neuropathic pain, the mechanisms of Treg–neuron interactions remain poorly defined.

pmc-13422923.creator: Malou Crasborn, Maarten O van Aken, Sam van Smoorenburg, Bas L van der Hoeven, Sytske van Bruggen, Mattijs E Numans, Rianne M C Pepping, Hedwig M M Vos, The Hague Consortium Of Network CarE Redesign and Transition, (The Hague CONCERT), Petra G van Peet, Rimke C Vos

pmc-13538475.creator: Xufeng Tao, Xiaonan Zhang, Fangyue Guo, Yunshu Zhang, Lei Zhang, Han Yu, Deshi Dong, Dong Shang, Hong Xiang

pmc-13582100.title: Pilot development with preliminary validation of a skills suturing score: essential suturing skills
pmc-13582100.creator: Renato V. Soares, Marina S. Guérios, Fernanda Tsumanuma, Fabiana A. Andrade
pmc-13582100.description: IntroductionSuturing skills are paramount for all surgeons. To date, there is no unified validated score that correlates with basic suturing abilities. We sought to develop and validate a score (Essential Suturing Skills—ESS) to evaluate basic suturing performance.MethodsThe ESS testing comprises two exercises.

pmc-13586885.title: Program-Level Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Use and 10-Year Survival in Advanced Ovarian Cancer
pmc-13586885.creator: Alex E. R. Powers, Gretchen Davis, Deshae Jenkins, Alicia Youssef, William Manning, Jason D. Wright, Nancy L. Keating, Amy Bregar, Alejandro Rauh-Hain, Alexander Melamed
pmc-13586885.description: This comparative effectiveness research examines the association between neoadjuvant chemotherapy adoption by US cancer programs and 10-year survival among patients with advanced ovarian cancer. Introduction Advanced-stage epithelial ovarian cancer is managed with cytoreductive surgery and platinum-based chemotherapy, although the optimal treatment sequencing remains debated.

pmc-13628651.title: Clinical Failure After Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair Mechanisms, Outcomes, and Management
pmc-13628651.creator: Paul Sorajja, Siddharth Singh, Robert Burke, Philip Gideon, Kenith Fang, David Rizik
pmc-13628651.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Transcatheter repair with edge-to-edge therapy (M-TEER) has been a revolutionary technology for patients with mitral regurgitation (MR). M-TEER is an established safe and effective treatment that alleviates MR, improves quality of life, and, in some patients, improves survival. Nonetheless, a significant number of M-TEER may not have procedural nor clinical success due to a variety of factors, with residual MR and/or mitral stenosis.

pmc-13633523.title: Closer matching between flow diverter diameter and parent artery diameter is associated with improved aneurysm occlusion
pmc-13633523.creator: Yoshimasa Fukui, Takashi Fujii, Kunihiro Matsumoto, Shuta Maehara, Kousei Maruyama, Kousuke Takigawa, Masahiro Yasaka, Hiroshi Aikawa, Yoshinori Go, Hidenori Oishi, Kiyoshi Kazekawa
pmc-13633523.description: Background: Selecting the flow diverter (FD) size is key to treatment outcomes in unruptured intracranial aneurysms. However, the impact of differences between the nominal and actual deployed device sizes on aneurysm occlusion is not fully understood. This study retrospectively evaluated the relationship between FD size and aneurysm occlusion.
